To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD4+ T lymphocytes are capable of inhibiting the outgrowth of lymphoblasts in vitro and the ability of CD8+ T lymphocytes to lyse lymphoblasts is contact‐dependent.
CD4+ T cell lines from different donors showed considerable variation in their cytokine production and capacity to inhibit the long term growth of autologus lymphoblastoid lines.
(1) CD4+ T lymphocytes can be cytotoxic towards autlogous LCL, and (2) this cytotoxicity is contact‐dependent and not mediated by cytokines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of CD4+ and cytotoxic T lymphocytes in the control of EBV‐induced lymphomas.
the role of EBV‐specific T cells in the pathogenesis of Burkitt's lymphoma (BL).
the role of CD4+ and cytotoxic T‐cell subsets in the control of EBV infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ability to inhibit autologou LCL growth in vitro is dependent upon the ability to induce apoptosis.
the capacity to inhibit LCL growth is dependent on the balance of Th1/Th0 and Th2/Th0 cells, and the balance between IFNγ, IL‐4 and IL‐13 production.

the ability of EBV‐specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes to inhibit the growth of autologus LCLs in culture is not dependent on the cytokines produced, but rather is a consequence of the killing of target cells by the cytotoxic T lymphocyte.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ability of activated CD4+ T lymphocytes to kill autologous lymphoma cell lines in vitro is not related to their ability to inhibit outgrowth in long‐term culture.
CD4+ T cell responses to LCL in vitro are complex, with the capacity for both growth inhibition and promotion of LCL outgrowth.
CD4+ T cell lines can be generated which inhibit the outgrowth of LCL in vitro, but these cells do not necessarily have a Th1 or Th2 phenotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD4+ T cell lines from different donors vary considerably in their ability to suppress the long‐term in vitro growth of autologously derived LCL.
EBV‐specific T cells are cytolytic, and that the killing is contact‐dependant.
CD4+ T cell lines from different donors have a wide range of cytokine production patterns, and that these do not correlate with the ability to inhibit autologouls LCL in vitro.
